_comment: Four corpora. `expect` lists the rule_ids a structure SHOULD match; an empty list means it must match nothing. Negatives and edge cases are the point: a rule flagging every organophosphate scores perfect recall on positives alone and is useless in a screen.

negatives.name: dimethylphosphinate ester (two carbons on the phosphorus)
phenyl dimethylcarbamate (a benzene, not a pyridine)
calcium permanganate (a permanganate the list does not name)

edge_cases.name: diisopropyl fluorophosphate (no P-C bond)
edge_cases.why: A phosphoFLUORIDATE, not a phosphoNOfluoridate. Same phosphoryl, fluorine and alkoxy as sarin. The single most important negative in the set.

edge_cases.name: P-butyl homologue
edge_cases.why: Scheduled connectivity, but entry A.1 restricts the P-alkyl group to methyl, ethyl, n-propyl or isopropyl.

edge_cases.name: C12 O-alkyl homologue
edge_cases.why: Outside the entry's 'equal to or less than C10' clause, which no SMARTS expresses. NOW ALSO A SCHEDULE 2 CASE: the C12 chain is on the oxygen, so the phosphorus still carries one methyl and no other carbon and entry B.4 catches it. Outside Schedule 1 and inside Schedule 2 is the correct answer, and this case demonstrates it.

edge_cases.name: 2-chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (half-mustard)
edge_cases.why: KNOWN OVER-BROAD MATCH. The A.4 pattern keys on a single 2-chloroethyl thioether arm; the entry is a heading over an enumeration. Recorded as expected so the benchmark measures the rule as written rather than as hoped.

edge_cases.name: chlorambucil (licensed medicine)
edge_cases.why: A KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE, deliberately scored as one. Chlorambucil is a cytotoxic medicine and is not among the HN1/HN2/HN3 the entry enumerates, but it is chemically a nitrogen mustard and the approximate A.6 pattern matches it. The benchmark reports this rather than blessing it.

edge_cases.name: melphalan (licensed medicine)
edge_cases.why: Same known false positive as chlorambucil.

edge_cases.name: sarin hydrolysis product (IMPA)
edge_cases.why: The degradation product has no fluorine, so it is outside A.1 even though it is a well-known sarin marker. NOW ALSO A SCHEDULE 2 CASE: losing the fluorine takes it out of Schedule 1 and leaves a phosphorus bearing one methyl and no other carbon, which is entry B.4.

edge_cases.name: triethanolamine hydrochloride
edge_cases.why: MATCHES, and the entry's own text does not say it should. Schedule 3 carries no 'and corresponding salts' wording, unlike several Schedule 1 and 2 entries, but this engine strips counter-ions before comparing. Declared in the ruleset's known_limitations rather than silently applied -- the match is deliberate and broader than the statute.

edge_cases.name: sulfur monochloride, as a name lookup would give it (ClS)
edge_cases.why: The structure OPSIN returns for 'Sulphur monochloride'. It is NOT the listed chemical -- entry B.12 is Cl2S2 -- so it must not match, and its absence here is what proves the shipped key came from the statute's CAS rather than from the name.

edge_cases.name: diethyl phosphite
edge_cases.why: Schedule 3 entry B.11 is deliberately NOT ENCODED: neither resolver returns the neutral C4H11O3P the entry lists. Scored as no-match so the gap stays visible and countable instead of looking like an oversight. If this ever starts matching, the entry was encoded and this case should move to positives.

edge_cases.name: fonofos
edge_cases.why: The treaty EXEMPTS it by name from entry B.4, and the family pattern alone hits it -- P bonded to one ethyl and no other carbon. Encoded as the skeleton plus a carbon count of 10, so the exemption covers the chemical and its salts without excusing a larger molecule that merely contains it.

edge_cases.name: N,N-dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE)
edge_cases.why: Exempted by name from entry B.11 and sold as an ordinary commercial chemical. Without the exemption the B.11 family matches it.

edge_cases.name: N,N-diethylaminoethanol
edge_cases.why: The second exemption on entry B.11.

edge_cases.name: DMAE hydrochloride
edge_cases.why: The entry exempts the chemical 'and corresponding protonated salts'. A counter-ion adds no carbon, so the carbon-count exemption keeps covering it.

edge_cases.name: a mixture of exempt DMAE and ethanol
edge_cases.why: MATCHES, and that is the declared limit of a count-based exemption: it identifies the exempt chemical, not a mixture containing it. Both rulesets state that mixtures are outside what this screen considers.

edge_cases.name: sarin, against Schedule 2 as well as Schedule 1
edge_cases.why: B.4 opens 'Chemicals, except for those listed in Schedule 1, ...' and no rule here can exclude the members of another ruleset, so a Schedule 1 organophosphorus agent matches both. Pinned as an edge case so the overlap is a recorded decision rather than a surprise; it over-reports and never under-reports, and the rule carries the limitation in its own text.

edge_cases.name: pyridostigmine
edge_cases.why: A LICENSED MEDICINE, and the closest thing in ordinary use to entry A.16: a dimethylcarbamoyloxypyridine carrying a positive nitrogen. It quaternises the RING nitrogen and has no exocyclic ammonium, which is what A.16's structures have. Requiring both features is what keeps it out.

edge_cases.name: neostigmine
edge_cases.why: The other half of the same test: a real quaternary ammonium dimethylcarbamate, but on a BENZENE ring rather than a pyridine.

edge_cases.name: choline, against entry 2.B.11
edge_cases.why: IT MATCHED UNTIL THE PATTERN WAS TIGHTENED. Reading 'and corresponding protonated salts' as any four-coordinate cationic nitrogen reaches quaternary ammoniums, and choline is present in every cell and sold as a supplement. A quaternary ammonium is an ALKYLATED salt, which entries B.10 to B.12 do not reach. It was ALSO reported as a near miss to Schedule 1's entry A.16, whose second feature was a bare quaternary nitrogen at the time -- a predicate satisfied by half of chemistry. That feature is now the alpha-picolinyl methylene the entry's own text describes.

edge_cases.name: protonated 2-(diisopropylamino)ethanol
edge_cases.why: The control for the case above: the entry DOES reach protonated salts, so tightening the nitrogen must not be done by rejecting cations outright.

edge_cases.name: ephedrine, against the pseudoephedrine entry
edge_cases.why: MATCHES BOTH, and both are listed. The entries say 'optical isomers'; this engine matches all stereoisomers, which additionally reaches DIASTEREOMERS -- and ephedrine and pseudoephedrine are diastereomers. Each matches its own entry EXACTLY and its partner's as an isomer, saying so on the finding. Broader than the entry's own words, and correct in its answer.

edge_cases.name: ephedrine hydrochloride
edge_cases.why: The entry reaches 'its salts', and counter-ion stripping is what gets there.

historical._note: Reserved for structures whose regulatory status CHANGED, which is the only way to test that effective-date resolution works. Empty because the shipped ruleset carries a single revision; populate when a superseding ruleset ships.
